sections.h2: What are my choices when I want to sell a house in Gurnee?
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it on your own, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer, and in every case the deed is recorded with the Lake County Clerk. Which one fits depends on the house's condition, how soon you need to close and whether you can carry costs while it sits on the market.

  • Listing: best for a house in good repair, since buyers with mortgages bring inspections and repair requests.
  • Selling yourself: saves on agent fees, but you handle showings, disclosures and the contract.
  • As-is cash sale: shortens the timeline and leaves repairs with the buyer, usually at a lower price.

Gurnee's visitor attractions are well known, but a house sale here is priced against nearby homes, so gather recent local sales before you set an asking price.

sections.h2: What kind of village is Gurnee?
sections.html:
Gurnee is a Lake County village on the Des Plaines River, about 40 miles north of Chicago and 50 miles south of Milwaukee. It borders Waukegan, was founded in 1928 and takes its name from Walter S. Gurnee, a former Chicago mayor and railroad director. The village covers about 13.5 square miles.

Interstate 94, the Tri-State Tollway, runs straight through and divides Gurnee into an older east side and a newer west side. Pace buses connect the village to Waukegan and Grayslake, and the CPKC main line between Chicago and Minneapolis serves it. Warren-Newport Public Library is the village's library district.

Settlers first arrived in the 1830s, and the hamlet was first called Wentworth before the railroad station took the Gurnee name. The old Mother Rudd House, a former stagecoach stop, now houses the Warren Township Historical Society.

sections.h2: How does tourism shape the Gurnee economy?
sections.html:
Tourism is the headline industry. Six Flags Great America opened in 1976 as Marriott's Great America, and its water park followed in 2005. Gurnee Mills, which opened in 1991, is the fourth largest mall in Illinois, and the Great Wolf Lodge resort opened in 2007. The village counts around 23 million visitors a year, and the parks are among its largest revenue sources.

Corporate employers include High Sierra Sport Company and PurposeBuilt Brands, the owner of Goo Gone. The Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales in Gurnee of about $1.4 billion, or $46,148 per resident.

Buyers will want to know how close a house sits to the I-94 corridor and the attraction areas, so be ready to describe its location.

sections.html:
Gurnee had an estimated 30,458 residents on July 1, 2025, compared with 30,706 counted in the 2020 census.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 census show about Gurnee households?
sections.html:
The census counted 11,900 households and 8,080 families in Gurnee, with 31.6 percent of households raising children under 18. The median age was 41.8, and 15.3 percent of residents were 65 or older. About 27 percent of households were one person living alone.

The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.2 percent and the rental vacancy rate 5.3 percent. Education and income run high: 56.7 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 67.9 percent of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

Gurnee has two elementary districts and one high school district. Most of the eastern half is in Gurnee School District 56, whose schools are Spaulding (pre-K to grade 2), Prairie Trail (grades 3 to 5), Viking Middle School (grades 6 to 8) and River Trail (kindergarten to grade 8).

  • Woodland Community Consolidated District 50 serves the western section and part of the east side, through Woodland Primary, Elementary, Intermediate and Middle schools.
  • Warren Township High School District 121 covers the whole village, with freshmen and sophomores at the O'Plaine Road campus and juniors and seniors at the Almond Road campus.
  • Prairie Crossing Charter School serves kindergarten through grade 8 for students in Districts 50 and 79.

Tell buyers which elementary district the house falls in, because the east and west sides differ.

sections.h2: What flood and permit issues should a Gurnee seller expect?
sections.html:
Flooding is the item buyers ask about most. In May 2004 heavy rain caused the worst flooding in 100 years, closing schools and damaging dozens of homes and businesses. The Village says its most dangerous flood hazard area is the low ground around the Des Plaines River and its tributaries.

  • Check your address on the Federal Insurance Rate Map and the inundation map the Village publishes.
  • Newer basements must have a sump pump ejection system, and the Village encourages backup systems.
  • Elevation certificates on file can be requested from the Engineering Division at 847-599-7550.
  • The Village takes part in the Community Rating System, which gives flood insurance discounts of 5 to 20 percent.

On permits, most construction and remodeling projects need a building permit before work starts, and the Village notes that permits can help prevent issues in future property sales. Fences, reroofs, siding, water heaters, furnaces and window replacements go through the online One Stop portal. Inspections need 24 hours' notice by calling the Building Division at 847-599-7550.

Two further Village programs are worth asking about. A voluntary floodplain buyout program is listed among its flooding resources, and a flood information mailing list sends updates to residents. Windows are a common permit item, and the Village's checklist sets a maximum residential U-factor of 0.28 for replacement windows and 0.30 for doors, so keep the contractor's contract on file if you replaced them.

sections.h2: What do I do about water service and the deed in Gurnee?
sections.html:
Gurnee gets its water from Lake Michigan through the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency. The Village's utility page, titled Start, Stop or Make Changes, is where you request a change to your account, so use it to close your service as the sale date nears.

The deed is recorded with the Lake County Clerk's recording division in Waukegan. The Clerk's deed packet says a deed must be dated, signed and notarized, name the parties, carry the buyer's address and a complete legal description, and list the preparer, a mail-to address and the name and address for tax bills. Every deed also needs a completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement.

The packet names Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago as the municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Gurnee is not on that list, but confirm with the Village before closing.

faqs.q: Where is a Gurnee deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Lake County Clerk's recording division in Waukegan, because Gurnee is in Lake County. The deed needs a notarized grantor signature, a legal description and either a PTAX-203 or an exemption statement.

faqs.q: Does Gurnee require a local transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's deed packet lists six municipalities that do, and Gurnee is not among them. Check with the Village if you want confirmation for your closing date.

faqs.q: Where can I find flood history for a Gurnee house?
faqs.a: Start with the Village. It publishes flood maps, keeps elevation certificates and historical flood information on file, and answers questions at 847-599-7550.

faqs.q: Which Gurnee schools will buyers ask about?
faqs.a: Most homes feed either Gurnee District 56 on the east side or Woodland District 50 on the west, and all feed Warren Township High School District 121. Look up your address before you describe the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gurnee house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes. The Village's permit page says permits can help prevent issues in future property sales, so ask the Building Division about your house's permit record. An as-is buyer can take a house without one.
